question: A starts traveling at 4 km/h. After 2 hours, B starts from the same place in the same direction at 6 km/h. How many hours after B starts will B catch up with A? (Unit: hours)
solution: For this catch-up problem, let B catch up with A \(t\) hours after B starts. Then \(6t=4(t+2)\). Solving gives \(t=4\).

reference.question: A starts traveling at 4 km/h. After 2 hours, B starts from the same place in the same direction at 6 km/h. How many hours after B starts will B catch up with A? (Unit: hours)
reference.solution:
Method 1: Equal-distance equation

For this catch-up problem, let B catch up with A \(t\) hours after B starts. Then \(6t=4(t+2)\). Solving gives \(t=4\).

Method 2: Closing the head start

When B starts, A is \(4\times2=8\) km ahead. Each hour, B travels \(6-4=2\) km farther than A, so the gap shrinks by \(2\) km. It therefore takes \(8\div2=4\) hours after B starts to close the gap.
